transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I've started doing things lately at work and school that just... don't really make sense. 

Like, at my bookkeeping job, I'll catch myself lining receipts all the way across the floor. Or I'll just sit there tapping the calculator, always in sets of nine. And the other day, I was just standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I just stayed like that until someone finally asked if I was okay. 

I don't really know why I'm doing these things, but it's weird, and I figured I should probably talk to a doctor about it.
When you do these things, does it feel like you have to do them to relieve anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

No, it's not really like that. I don't feel anxious before I do them, and I'm not worried about something bad happening if I don't. It's more like... I just find myself doing it. There's no real reason or feeling behind it, it just kind of happens.
Have you been feeling unusually high, energetic, or euphoric lately?

Yeah, actually. Some weeks I feel... just unusually sharp. Almost unstoppable, I guess. Like I have so much energy I can sit down and map out my whole future in just one night. 

But it's kind of a double-edged sword, because during those same times, if my boss or a classmate makes even a small correction to something I did, I get really on edge. I'll end up snapping at them a lot harder than I mean to.
During those high-energy times, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, actually. I've gone a few nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours. But I don't feel tired the next day at all. I still feel totally ready to go to work and class. It honestly just feels like sleeping is a waste of time when I could be getting everything figured out instead.
Do these unusual behaviors mainly happen during the times when you feel unusually energized and need very little sleep?

No, not just then. Like, there was a stretch of a few weeks recently where I was sleeping a normal amount and didn't have all that extra energy, but... I was still hearing the voice. And I still felt really pulled into those number patterns, even without the high energy.
When you end up staying in one position like that, are you unable to move even if you want to?

Well, it's not that I'm physically frozen or can't move my muscles. It's more that... I just start doing things at work and school that don't make any sense, and I get stuck doing them. 

Like, I'll stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I'll just stay in that position until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay. That's actually the main reason I came in to see you. I've been doing other weird stuff too, like taking receipts and lining them all across the floor, or just sitting at my desk tapping the calculator in sets of nine. So I can move, I just... end up doing these bizarre things instead.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice even though you weren’t feeling unusually energized or needing less sleep?

Yeah, like I was just saying a minute ago, it was a stretch of a few weeks recently. So... yeah, definitely at least two weeks. I was sleeping my normal hours and didn't have all that extra energy, but the voice was still there.
Have you had any recent medical illness or neurologic problem?
No, I haven't had anything like that. I've been pretty healthy, physically, anyway. No illnesses or head injuries or anything like that recently.
When you hear the voice, does it tell you that you have special powers or an important mission?

No, it doesn't say anything like that. It's just the one voice, and it mostly just talks about what I'm doing or... or tells me to do those weird things I mentioned, like lining up the receipts. It never says anything about special powers or missions or anything grand like that.
